questions.text:
Directions: A statement is given followed by two inferences I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems to be at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given inferences, if any, follow from the given statement.

Statement: It is really mocking for the largest democratic country to retain the tag of developing nations for so long.

Inference:

I. India yet has to become a developed nation.

II.Unless, we change our perception India cannot become developed.
questions.explanation:
Correct option 1.Only inference I follows.

The statement suggests that despite being the largest democracy in the world, India is still classified as a developing country.

From the statement, it can be deduced that India is progressive and has yet to become a developed nation. Therefore, Inference I follows.

But since the statement does not discuss the parameters of development and the criteria to assess development. We cannot deduce that a change in the perception will help India become developed. Therefore, Inference II does not follow.

Hence, option 1 is correct.

questions.text:
Directions: Two statements are followed by two Conclusions 1 and 2. You have to consider the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. You are to decide which of the following conclusions can definitely be drawn from the given statements and indicate your answer accordingly.

Statements:

I: Fluoride makes the enamel of your teeth harder and more resistant to acid wear. Doctors advise using it externally to help in fighting tooth decay and cavities.

II: Though, any fluoride-rich food contains more than 5 mg, the prescribed limit of fluoride intake is not more than 2 mg a day.

Conclusions:

1: Fluoride-rich foods, if consumed daily, can help us get rid of the daily need of brushing our teeth.

2: Toothpaste rich in fluoride can prevent the wear and tear of teeth.
questions.explanation:
The first statement mentions about making the enamel of our teeth stronger and brings forward its benefits over tooth decay and cavities.

The first conclusion does not follow as eating fluoride-rich food regularly could mean that one would cross the prescribed limit.
Hence, conclusion 1 does not follow.

Since toothpaste is used externally, its usage will not cross the prescribed limit and also give the benefits mentioned in the statements. Thus, it will help prevent the wear and tear of teeth.
Hence, conclusion 2 follows.

Thus, only conclusion 2 follows.

ED = 10 m

Direction: In the following question assuming the given statements to be true, find which of the conclusion among given some conclusion is/are definitely true and then give your answers accordingly:

Statement:

F > D > I < A ≤ E ≤ W < O ≥ Q > P = T > J < L > M

Conclusions:

I. F > W 

II. W > P

III. P < M

options.text: Both  Conclusion I and II is True
None of the Conclusion is True

questions.explanation:
Given Statement:

F > D > I < A ≤ E ≤ W < O ≥ Q > P = T > J < L > M

Conclusions:

I. F > W → False (F > D > I < A ≤ E ≤ W, as definite relationship between F and W cannot be determined).

II. W > P → False (W < O ≥ Q > P, as definite relationship between W and P cannot be determined).

III. P < M → False (P = T > J < L > M, as definite relationship between P and M cannot be determined).

Hence, None of the Conclusion is True.
